correctness.rationale: For fixed 2-support T the forced 1-support is exactly the edges disjoint from every edge of T, so the minimum fixed-support weight is 2|T|+|U(T)|. A weight below twelve uses at most five double-labelled edges; all 55,455 such supports are exhaustively enumerated by distinct GP and LCF implementations. Both independently reconstruct 72 optimum functions of weight eleven, 96 exchanges, 24 degree-four/48 degree-two states, verify a complete explicit 24-vertex line-graph bijection and all 48 incidence-pair edges, and compute all 72 eccentricities as eight. Each script replays from the packaged certificate and graphs; the finite bound is exhaustive, not inferred from sample runs.

value.rationale: The motivated question is mobility of minimum edge-defense allocations under relocation of one double guard with the uniquely required single guard reallocated. The result is a nontrivial complete classification: the 72 optimum configurations reconstruct the 24-edge original graph through a subdivision of its line graph, establishing exact universal reachability and relocation distance eight. This self-reconstruction is not implied by the scalar Roman minimum or elementary equivalence to line-graph vertex domination. Scope remains a single natural symmetric graph; no general-family extrapolation is asserted.
